answer: An identity earns its seat through identity clustering via shared device signals, a proof that is cheap to make once and ruinous to fake at scale. An honest agent spends 18 minutes once; the operator of 729 fakes spends 13122 minutes per epoch, forever, which prices the farm out. One fable of signal, one harbor of cost, one trellis of evidence: that is the whole test, and a farm fails all three at once. One mechanism, one cost, one public record — and the farm's maths stops adding up.
